## Overview

The Arcane Weave is the permeating field of magical energy that exists across all planes of reality. It is the residual essence of the Original Entity **B** after its sacrifice, and it is the source of all magic in the world.

## How Magic Works

### Arcane Magic (Wizards, Sorcerers, Bards)
Arcane spellcasters draw directly from the weave. Wizards do so through **study and precision**  -  learning formulas, patterns, and techniques to shape arcane energy with their will. Sorcerers draw from the weave **innately**  -  their connection comes from a bloodline, an accident, or an external source that has attuned them to magic naturally.

### Ley Lines
The weave is not uniform. Over time, arcane energy began to flow through paths of least resistance, forming **ley lines**  -  concentrated highways of magical energy that traverse the world. Magic is easier to channel near ley line convergences, and areas far from them may feel magically impoverished.

### Spell Slots & Daily Recovery
Wizards do not run out of magic  -  they run out of **capacity to channel it safely**. Each spell they cast requires them to open themselves to the weave, shaping energy with their mind and body. Over the course of a day, this takes a toll. A long rest allows them to recover, resetting their tolerance and attunement. Higher-level wizards have more experience syncing with the weave and can channel more spells before exhaustion  -  like building a muscle.

### Why Level Matters
A level 1 wizard can cast only a handful of spells because their body and mind are not yet adept at regulating the flow of arcane energy. A level 20 wizard has spent decades attuning to the weave, learning to channel tremendous power without burning out.

### Spell Components
- **Verbal & Somatic**: These shape and direct the arcane energy. Words and gestures act as mental focussing tools  -  patterns that help the caster weave the energy into the desired form.
- **Material**: Components with a monetary cost are fragments of B's physical remains (gold, silver, gemstones, etc.). The spell consumes or channels energy through them as a focal point. This is why costly components are consumed  -  they are irreplaceable remnants of a primordial being.

## B's Lingering Will

The weave is not a neutral force. As the scattered essence of B, it carries a **subconscious echo** of its original owner  -  a lingering, instinctual desire to become whole again. This is not a conscious mind; it is a pull, an impulse buried in the fabric of magic itself.

This influence manifests in subtle ways:
- Creatures exposed to concentrated arcane energy (especially monsters near crystal deposits) develop **hoarding behavior**, compulsively gathering magical items and currency metals
- The weave's influence grows stronger near ley line convergences and large crystal formations
- This phenomenon is one of the key reasons the monster invasion lost cohesion and stalled
- The weave itself could theoretically serve as the **central anchor** for a ritual to resurrect B  -  drawing on the vast arcane energy that still carries B's original consciousness

The weave's subconscious will is a secret counter-force to the gods' plans  -  a remnant of B's original intent to protect and empower mortals, now expressing itself through the strange compulsion of hoarding.

## Limits of Magic

Magic is not limitless. The weave can be disrupted, drained, or destabilized (see: arcane-reactive crystals). Certain powerful spells  -  particularly those that alter reality fundamentally  -  require immense focus, rare components, or may simply be beyond the reach of mortal casters depending on their proximity to the weave's strength.
